901a6763ae290789: KUALA LUMPUR: Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd's 16 per cent valuation premium over Bursa Malaysia-listed discretionary consumer peers leaves limited room for further upside, CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said.
The research house initiated coverage on the fixed-price retailer with a "Hold" call and RM1.50 target price, saying the stock is fairly priced as its growth prospects have largely been factored in.
Eco-Shop last closed at RM1.45, valuing the company at RM8.35 billion. At the time of writing, the stock remained at RM1.45.
CIMB Securities said Eco-Shop trades at 24.1 times calendar year 2027 forecast earnings, considerably higher than several discretionary names under the firm's coverage.
By comparison, Mr DIY Group (M) Bhd trades at 17 times, while Aeon Co (M) Bhd is valued at 7.7 times, Padini Holdings Bhd at 7.6 times and Bonia Corp Bhd at 10.2 times.
MyNews Holdings Bhd trades at 15.3 times, Amway (Malaysia) Holdings Bhd at 14.3 times and Empire Premium Food Bhd at 15 times.
At the higher end, 7-Eleven Malaysia Holdings Bhd trades at 51.5 times 2027 forecast earnings.
The premium comes as Eco-Shop is forecast to deliver stronger earnings growth than the discretionary peer group.

CIMB Securities forecasts Eco-Shop's earnings per share to grow 22.2 per cent in 2026 and 18.4 per cent in 2027, against the discretionary peer group's weighted average growth of 8.6 per cent and 10.4 per cent, respectively.
Analyst Walter Aw Lik Hsin said Eco-Shop's strong sourcing capabilities, proven value retail proposition and continued network expansion provide a solid foundation for earnings growth.

Nevertheless, he said near-term upside could be capped by execution risks surrounding its expansion plans, a potential moderation in same-store sales growth and margin pressure from rising sourcing requirements and operating expenses.
The research firm's initiation comes as value-focused retailers are relatively better placed to weather cautious consumer spending.
Eco-Shop's revenue rose 12.2 per cent year-on-year to RM772.9 million in its fourth quarter ended May 2026, while core net profit rose 44.9 per cent to RM72.6 million.
CIMB Securities said value retailers such as Eco-Shop and Mr DIY were relatively better positioned as consumers increasingly prioritise affordability and trade down to cheaper alternatives.
The firm expects this trend to persist in the near term, although higher operating and sourcing costs could continue to put pressure on margins.
b8060009828ab78a: KUALA LUMPUR: The armed forces are ready to deploy air assets to support the Health Ministry's Flying Doctor Service (FDS) following its suspension after a recent helicopter crash.

Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the military would coordinate with the Health Ministry and other agencies to provide airlift support, particularly for emergency cases involving people in remote areas who require immediate medical treatment.
"The armed forces, through the Royal Malaysian Air Force, are prepared to coordinate requests for assistance based on the availability of its air assets.

"We are willing to contribute; there is no problem. We will coordinate. We have the assets; just table the request, the demand, and so on, and then we will respond. This is a shared responsibility for us during peacetime," he said during an interview ahead of the 93rd Armed Forces Day celebration.

Malek said the armed forces regularly assist with airlift requests, particularly in emergency cases where individuals who have suffered injuries require immediate evacuation from remote areas for medical treatment.

"These also include transporting people from Sabah and Sarawak to Kuala Lumpur when required, as such assistance was part of the armed forces' role as one of the service providers supporting other agencies and ministries under the concept of comprehensive security.
"However, when it involves routine medical services carried out by the Health Ministry (such as the Flying Doctor Service), previously we have not been involved in that kind of service.

"However, as a service provider, and one of the service providers involved in the context of collective security and comprehensive security, we support all agencies and other ministries if there is a requirement, especially to cover the gap during this crucial period when they are unable to operate because they do not have air assets," he said.
It was reported that the FDS in Sarawak will only resume after the investigation into the recent helicopter crash is completed and the Health Ministry is satisfied that operations are safe.

The Health Ministry said the temporary suspension of FDS operations would remain in place pending the outcome of the investigation, with the safety and welfare of healthcare workers remaining its top priority.
The ministry said it was carrying out a comprehensive audit covering service-location mapping, operator compliance with required standards, and the psychosocial needs of FDS personnel.
The temporary suspension involves seven FDS teams serving 85 localities, affecting an estimated population of about 14,830 people in Sarawak's interior.
1345b3893f91bb3a: BOGOTA, Sept 14 — Five people are missing after a small plane disappeared in northwestern Colombia, the country’s Civil Aviation Authority said yesterday, reported Xinhua.
The plane, which took off from Mandinga Airport in Condoto in the northwestern department of Choco, was bound for Guaymaral Airport in Bogota, the capital.
The last communication with the aircraft was recorded at 9.23am (10.23pm Malaysia time) local time, the authority said in a statement.
An emergency locator beacon was later activated near Cerro Tatama, about 33 nautical miles from the Pereira VOR navigation beacon.
Authorities said the search was being hampered by difficult access to the area. — Bernama-Xinhua
d1d2675d9b88f5ac: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is ready to deploy its air assets to assist the Health Ministry (MoH) in providing Flying Doctor Service (FDS), particularly for emergency medical evacuations in remote areas.
Chief of Defence Forces Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the move was aimed at meeting the ministry’s urgent needs following last Tuesday’s FDS helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak.
He said the MAF had sufficient facilities and helicopters to undertake the missions and was ready to cooperate once an official request was coordinated at ministry level.
“As a provider of services in the context of comprehensive security and emergency assistance, we will fill the gap during this critical period, particularly in areas that are difficult to access.

“We are ready to meet the ministry’s request and coordinate the operational efforts to ensure that services for the people are not disrupted,” he said during a special interview with the Chief of Defence Forces in conjunction with the 93rd MAF Day at Wisma Pertahanan here today.
Malek Razak, however, stressed that the MAF’s assistance would focus on emergency evacuation support and would not involve taking over the MoH’s routine medical operations in their entirety.
Yesterday, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said four government agencies, including the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), would assist the MoH in providing temporary mercy flights.

The alternative arrangement, which also involves the Royal Malaysia Police, Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency and Fire and Rescue Department, will remain in place pending the outcome of investigations and completion of safety improvements for FDS operations.
The BO-105 helicopter crash near the Long Lellang STOLport runway claimed five lives, including four MoH medical personnel.

The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Jessie Paya Jok, 44, and Debra Moset, 40. — Bernama
cef12675f65758d6: JOHANNESBURG: Algerian winger Mohamed Belloumi scored twice as promoted Hull City stretched an unbeaten Premier League run this season to four matches at the weekend by drawing 2-2 away to Chelsea.
AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues:
England
Mohamed Belloumi (Hull City)
Belloumi struck his first two league goals to continue Hull's honeymoon start to life back in the top flight after a 10-year absence.
He scored twice in six first-half minutes with two sweet strikes on his left foot, although his second goal benefited from multiple deflections off Chelsea defenders.
His brace secured a point for the third-placed Tigers at Stamford Bridge.
Malick Yalcouye (Brighton)
The Mali-born midfielder was on the scoresheet in the Seagulls' 5-0 rout of 10-man Coventry.

Yalcouye, who has played for the Ivory Coast under-23 team after being raised in the country, bagged Brighton's second goal in the 51st minute, accelerating away from the Coventry defence to fire home.
It was the 20-year-old's second goal this season after also netting in a defeat at Chelsea.
Spain
Inaki Williams (Athletic Bilbao)
Ghana international Williams snatched his team a 1-1 La Liga draw against Elche by scoring from close-range with little over 10 minutes remaining.
The 32-year-old striker got the lightest touch on the ball to brush it home while two defenders tried to block him. It was his first goal of the campaign.
Italy
Akor Adams (Venezia)
Adsms put bottom club Venezia ahead at home to Fiorentina, but a Franco Mastantuono hat-trick helped the visitors to a 4-2 Serie A victory.
The Nigeria striker unleashed a shot from just inside the box to bring temporary joy to the strugglers.
Germany
Christian Kofane (Bayer Leverkusn)
Kofane's classy 18th-minute strike was not enough as Leverkusen were held to a 2-2 draw at Augsburg.
The 20-year-old Cameroon striker collected a long pass from Burkinabe Edmond Tapsoba and cooly guided a low shot into the bottom right corner to open the scoring.
Serhou Guirassy (Borussia Dortmund)
Guirassy had two goals chalked off for offside, but still played a crucial role as Borussia sailed to a comfortable 3-0 home victory over Paderborn.
Named alongside strike partner Fabio Silva for the first time this season, Guirassy fed the Portuguese near the halfway line and Silva scored the opener after just five minutes.
France
Abdallah Sima (Lens)
Sima triggered a Lens comeback in a 2-2 Ligue 1 draw at Le Mans by scoring in added time at the end of the first half to halve a two-goal deficit.
The Senegal international claimed his first league this season with a header past goalkeeper Ewan Hatfout. — AFP

856d2f40c3856281: PETALING JAYA: Remaja lelaki berusia 15 tahun dilepas dan dibebaskan daripada pertuduhan membunuh rakan sekolahnya di SMK Bandar Utama Damansara (4) tahun lalu selepas Mahkamah Tinggi Shah Alam mendapati tertuduh tidak sempurna akal ketika melakukan kesalahan itu.
Hakim Adlin Abdul Majid memerintahkan remaja berkenaan ditahan dan menjalani rawatan di Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, Perak, atas perkenan Sultan Selangor, lapor Berita Harian.
Prosiding kes tersebut dijalankan secara tertutup di Mahkamah Tinggi kerana tertuduh adalah remaja bawah umur.

Peguam remaja itu, Kitson Foong memberitahu wartawan selepas prosiding itu, mahkamah mendapati syarat di bawah Seksyen 84 Kanun Keseksaan, yang memperuntukkan pembelaan atas alasan tidak sempurna akal, berjaya dibuktikan oleh pihak pembelaan dan pihak pendakwaan gagal menafikannya.

Timbalan pendakwa raya Syed Ahmed Khabir Abdul Rahman mewakili pihak pendakwaan.
b2743a4e25cae842: JERUSALEM: Israeli culture minister Miki Zohar has called for award-winning directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor to be stripped of their Israeli citizenship, accusing them of "treason against the state" over their documentary NAZA about Israel's war in Gaza.

The 80-minute film features interviews with 24 Israeli military and intelligence whistleblowers who describe AI-powered targeting systems allegedly used in Israeli bombardments of Gaza. The documentary won a Special Jury Prize at this year's Venice Film Festival.
Zohar accused the filmmakers of being willing to "harm their homeland in order to receive applause from antisemites around the world".
"I will act immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators for treason against the state," he said on X.
The directors have previously received international recognition for their work.
Abraham and Szor were among the filmmakers behind No Other Land, which won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature in 2025 and examined Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank.
Far-right national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir also attacked the pair, calling them "a disgrace and an embarrassment to the entire people of Israel".
"Go away!" he wrote on X, adding that Hamas would welcome them "with open arms".
Abraham defended the documentary and its findings, saying the Israeli intelligence officers interviewed described the killings in Gaza as systematic.
"Not by accident, but by design, actions of murder and policies that are based on the total dehumanisation of Palestinians," he said.
Israel's military has criticised the film's reliance on anonymous testimonies, saying the identities of the whistleblowers "cannot be verified".
Israel has also denied deliberately targeting civilians.
Stripping Israeli citizenship is legally possible but rarely used.

Under legislation upheld by the Supreme Court in 2022, citizenship can be revoked for acts including espionage or treason, while a 2023 expansion also covers convictions for terrorism. The process requires a request from the interior minister, approval by the justice minister and validation by judges.
d7c3421e7301a851: BUDAPEST: Most athletes might bristle at seeing their records being broken. When eight-time Olympic champion Usain Bolt learned that a robot in China had eclipsed his 100-metres world record by almost a second, he was rather amused by the turn of events.
"It's just one of those things. I guess that's where the world is going right now," the Jamaican said with a laugh and a shrug. "It just made me smile."

A couple of weeks ago, "Robot beats Bolt" was splashed across headlines after Tiangong Ultra won the 100m final at the second ⁠World Humanoid Robot Games, clocking 8.64 seconds, almost a second faster than Bolt's 9.58 world-record set in 2009.

The 40-year-old Bolt was in relaxed form as he met reporters in Budapest on the final day of the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship, delivering a stream of anecdotes and one-liners that showed why he remains one of athletics' most magnetic personalities.
Although from the outset, Bolt appeared keen to wrap things up early.
"United is playing right now (versus City in the Manchester derby)," said the lifelong Manchester United supporter. "Very important time."
Bolt also reflected on his place in sporting history and how he hoped to be remembered, saying his ambition was never simply to dominate athletics, but to transcend it.

"My goal was always to be among the greats in sports," he said. "That when the conversation is being talked about Muhammad Ali ... and all these greats in different sports, I'm mentioned in that sentence. I'm happy that I'm actually in the conversation."
Bolt scolded reporters who had suggested at last year's world championships in Tokyo that he was out of shape.

"First of all, I made a joke and you guys took it out of context. It was everywhere!" he said. "I wasn't running out of breath walking up the stairs. I was just making a joke. I'm in the best shape of my life, guys."
His declaration drew laughter around the room.
"Listen, 'he's in the best shape of his life'. That's the headline," he said laughing before adding that he still works out daily.
Bolt flirted with a football career, but it ended in 2018 after a two-month trial with Australian club Central Coast Mariners, where he scored twice in a friendly on his first start.
But he had no answer for how his name was recently linked to Wythenshawe Vets FC, a Sunday league team in south Manchester that has gained attention for recruiting former Premier League players.
While Wythenshawe's supposed superstar signing made headlines, Bolt insisted he first learned about it when his longtime agent Ricky Simms contacted him.
"Ricky texted me and said, 'Are you playing football now?' And I was like, 'I don't know what's going on'."
Simms offered his own explanation.
"I think they wanted to have the option if he's ever in Manchester and wants to play."

And if any non-league club is still holding out hope of signing the fastest man in history, Bolt sounded in no rush to dust off his boots, preferring instead to keep an eye on Manchester United and enjoy retirement. — REUTERS

5a126145d0372185: KUALA LUMPUR: Pas has demanded an explanation from the government over the deferment of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon application.
Its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the matter was of public interest and warranted an immediate explanation.
In a statement today, he questioned the circumstances surrounding the deferment, which was announced on Sept 11 by the Prime Minister's Department's Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU).

"Pas believes the deferment of Datuk Seri Najib's application before the Pardons Board would not have occurred on its own unless there was a directive or objection from either members of the board or other interested third parties," he said.
Takiyuddin said the circumstances surrounding the deferment should therefore be made clear to the public.
"Pas demands that the government immediately explain the matter to the public as it is an issue of public interest that should not be withheld from the people," he said.
The Prime Minister's Department had previously said Najib's application would be deferred to a future Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) meeting.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had also consented to the deferment of Najib's application to a future FTPB meeting.

b4d5d56e1e71a492: BEIJING: Beijing will ban the possession of drones within city limits under new rules from November, further tightening regulations that already prohibited the sale of the devices.
The rules, announced on Sunday and due to take effect on Nov 15, forbid possessing or storing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in the Chinese capital and ban flights in its airspace.
Transporting drones or their components into Beijing will also be forbidden.
Airspace safety fears in the city of 22 million were raised in June when a small plane crashed into its tallest skyscraper, killing the pilot and injuring 13 others.
The regulations, formulated by Beijing's municipal government, cited the need to "safeguard the security of the capital".
Under rules introduced in May, Beijing already prohibited drone sales, while owners had to register their devices but were allowed to keep them.
The new regulations mandate that all drone owners dispose of their devices or move them out of Beijing by Nov 15, or else face confiscation and fines.
Authorities will offer subsidies for owners to scrap their gadgets or sell them through buy-back channels.
Alternatively, they will be offered free shipping to mail them out of the city.
Drone flights in Beijing's airspace already require permission from authorities.
According to the new rules, exemptions may be provided for special purposes like counter-terrorism, agriculture, disaster relief, and research.
e8da1ae8939f3f7f: PETALING JAYA: The teenage boy charged with killing a 16-year-old schoolmate at a school in Bandar Utama last year was acquitted after the Shah Alam High Court ruled that he was of unsound mind when the offence was committed.

Justice Adlin Abdul Majid nonetheless ordered the 15-year-old to be detained at the pleasure of the Selangor sultan at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak, where he will undergo treatment, Berita Harian reported.

The boy’s lawyer, Kitson Foong, said the court found the defence had proven that the accused was incapable of knowing the nature of the act or that it was contrary to law at the time the murder was committed.
c14003c82fb48789: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is conducting a budget tour to gather views and suggestions from industry players, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and members of the public nationwide as it prepares for Budget 2027.

Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the tour aims to gain insight into the needs of key sectors in each state and obtain input from parties directly affected by government policies and allocations.
“We are visiting every state to understand the industries that are important,” he told reporters after visiting Sekolah Menengah Agama Al-Mashoor (Girls) here today.
Amir Hamzah said Penang is among the locations due to its important role in the electrical and electronics (E&E) and semiconductor sectors.
The medical devices sector is also a focus of the Penang tour, given that Malaysia exports a wide range of medical equipment and is advanced in this industry, he said.
“This is one of the high-value economic sectors with the potential to boost domestic employment by creating better jobs here,” he said.
There will be a tour of Sabah and Perak before Penang to gather views from industry players, including those in the blue (maritime-based) economy and automotive sectors.
The government will study all views received through focus group sessions and meetings with stakeholders, he said, adding that some will be considered for inclusion in the budget.
The other proposals will be examined and discussed with the relevant ministries and agencies.

“The focus on specific groups has significantly contributed to enhancing the budget’s quality, given that we have looked beyond ministries and agencies to incorporate proposals from the industry, NGOs, and the public.
“This is to ensure that our budget is comprehensive and inclusive across all sectors,” he said. — Bernama
4cf5985c0814a4d5: DUBAI, Sept 14 — The number of international tourists visiting Dubai dropped by 44 per cent year-on-year in the first eight months of 2026 amid escalating tensions in West Asia, according to data from Dubai’s Economy and Tourism Department, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.

Ahead of the annual Arabian Travel Market exhibition in Dubai, officials released data on tourist numbers for the first time since February. Previously, such figures had been published on a monthly basis.
In the first eight months of 2026, the city welcomed 6.97 million international tourists, including 869,000 in August, the highest monthly figure since February, the Dubai Media Office said.
Monthly performance reports for Dubai’s tourism sector, available on the department’s website, show that 12.54 million tourists visited the city between January and August 2025.
Consequently, tourist arrivals fell by more than 44 per cent, representing a drop of nearly 5.6 million people in absolute terms.
In 2025, Dubai welcomed a record 19.6 million international tourists.
Dubai authorities aimed to transform the emirate into a year-round tourist destination and one of the world’s top three tourism hubs.
Amid regional tensions and flight cancellations after the escalation in February, many hotels in Dubai closed for renovations. — Bernama-Sputnik/RIA Novosti
7208e8b6988f1234: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has raised a former supermarket employee's eight-year jail term for killing a two-year-old child in his care to 20 years.
A three-member bench comprising Justices Noorin Badaruddin, Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid allowed the prosecution’s appeal against the sentence imposed on Noor Ab Manap, 36.
Noorin, who chaired the bench, said the eight-year term imposed by the High Court in Kuantan on Aug 19 last year was inadequate and failed to reflect the seriousness of the offence.
Noor was initially charged with murder, but the prosecution accepted his representation to reduce the charge to culpable homicide not amounting to murder. He pleaded guilty.
The father-of-four committed the offence in Kampung Janglau, Rompin, on Nov 11, 2021.
Delivering the judgment, Noorin said the child, identified as Adam, was entrusted to Noor and his wife for RM250 a month.
"This was not merely a relationship between two ordinary individuals," she said.
Noorin said this was an important aggravating factor because a child placed in an adult’s care was entitled to expect protection from the person responsible for looking after him.
"That trust was betrayed with the most tragic consequence – the loss of the child’s life," she said.
The court also took into account the nature and extent of Adam’s injuries.

Forensic findings showed that blunt-force trauma caused serious internal abdominal injuries, including mesenteric tears and internal bleeding. About 300ml of blood and clots were found in his abdominal cavity.
Noorin said the child’s physical vulnerability had to be considered, as force that might be regarded as moderate against an adult could have far more serious consequences for a small child.
She said there was also no evidence that Adam had provoked Noor.
The court acknowledged that Noor was a first-time offender who pleaded guilty, expressed remorse and had a family and four young children.
However, Noorin said a guilty plea was not an automatic entitlement to a particular reduction in sentence.
She also said Noor’s financial difficulties and stress could not be given excessive weight when he had other options, including seeking help or returning the child to his original guardian.
"The respondent had other choices," she said.
Deputy public prosecutor Solehah Noratikah Ismail appeared for the prosecution while Aida Rahayu Abdul Rahman and Amara Abu represented Noor.

67bfadbc72ed0d90: KUALA LUMPUR: Cyberbullying, which can occur continuously without time or geographical boundaries, increases the risk of self-harm among adolescents, particularly when combined with relationship conflicts, a psychiatrist said.

Universiti Malaya (UM) Faculty of Medicine Department of Psychological Medicine head and senior consultant psychiatrist Associate Professor Dr Muhammad Muhsin Ahmad Zahari said adolescents were undergoing complex biological, emotional and behavioural development.

He said the prefrontal cortex, which controls judgement and rational thinking, was not yet fully developed at that age, leaving adolescents more vulnerable to interpersonal crises involving peers, family members or partners.
"When interpersonal stress meets heightened emotional reactions caused by exposure to the digital world, their ability to make mature decisions can be severely affected.
"Interpersonal problems can also lead to bullying. Both victims and perpetrators are at high risk of developing mental disorders, which can lead to violent behaviour and suicide.
"Cyberbullying that occurs continuously without time or geographical boundaries increases the risk of suicidal behaviour, particularly among adolescents and children," he said when contacted today.
Muhsin was commenting on several recent incidents involving adolescents and students who reportedly fell from buildings, which have raised public concern.
He said physical and cyberbullying must be identified and addressed early as both victims and perpetrators could develop mental health problems.
Parents and teachers, he said, should be alert to changes in behaviour, sleeping patterns and emotional wellbeing.
He said homes and schools should provide safe spaces where young people could seek help without fear of being judged or punished.
"A punitive approach may cause them to bottle up their problems and become increasingly isolated," he said.
Muhsin said responses to bullying should not be limited to legal action, but should include psychological assessments, treatment and counselling for both victims and perpetrators.

He also called for more trained school counsellors capable of conducting risk assessments and crisis interventions, while urging greater attention to the shortage of child and adolescent psychiatry specialists.
b95ab29479c11ef0: KUALA LUMPUR: Kelington Group Bhd has secured a provisional US$452 million (RM1.83 billion) contract to provide turnkey total facility tool hookup services for a semiconductor wafer fabrication facility in Gujarat, India.
Kelington, an integrated engineering solutions provider, said its wholly-owned Kelington Engineering (S) Pte Ltd accepted a letter of award for the project.

The scope covers the overall design, installation, connection, testing and handover of manufacturing, laboratory and support tools, as well as related tool-specific support systems for Module 1 and Module 2 of the facility.
The works are expected to take 30 months, with completion targeted by February 2029.
The provisional contract value comprises US$249.9 million (RM1.01 billion) for Module 1 and US$202 million (RM817.2 million) for Module 2, covering up to 886 tools across both modules.
The group said the final contract value would be determined based on the actual quantities of tools and services executed.
Kelington chief executive officer Lim Seng Chuan said the project was the largest secured by the group since its establishment and validated its engineering capabilities and execution track record.
He said the award also marked an important step in Kelington's efforts to expand its capabilities as a main contractor for turnkey total facility tool hookup services in the semiconductor industry.
"The project provides us with an important platform to deepen our presence in the semiconductor industry and create opportunities for further growth," he said in a statement.
Lim said the latest contract followed an earlier award from the same client for a different scope of work.

He said turnkey total facility tool hookup was a critical part of bringing semiconductor manufacturing equipment into operation, requiring coordination across multiple engineering disciplines and stringent execution standards.
Lim said India was also making significant investments to develop its domestic semiconductor manufacturing capabilities, positioning Kelington to participate in the sector's growth.
"The scale of this award further strengthens our presence in the market and provides us with a solid foundation to pursue further opportunities as India's semiconductor ecosystem continues to expand.

"Together with our inclusion in the MSCI Malaysia Small Cap Index and our AAA rating by MSCI ESG Ratings, this award reflects the group's steady progress in building a stronger global profile through our expanding international footprint and growing visibility among global investors.

"In addition, we remain focused on executing the projects successfully, delivering value to our customer and shareholders, and building the capabilities required to compete for larger and more sophisticated projects globally," he noted.
For the six months ended June 30, 2026, the group secured RM1.23 billion in new contracts.
Including subsequent contract wins of RM538 million and the RM1.83 billion hookup contract, total year-to date wins stood at RM3.59 billion.
b65d50a30f1ddd50: SINGAPORE, Sept 14 — Transboundary smoke haze was observed over Singapore and extended as far as southern Vietnam today morning, the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) said.
In its daily weather and haze situation report, ASMC said the hotspot and haze situation in the region is expected to remain elevated, with a continued risk of transboundary smoke haze.

“The prevailing winds over the southern Asean region are forecast to blow mainly from the southeast, except for parts of Borneo where winds are forecast to be light and variable in direction,” it said today.
ASMC continued to detect moderate to dense smoke haze in central and southern Sumatra, West and Central Kalimantan, as well as parts of Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.

“Clusters of scattered hotspots were detected in the southern parts of Sumatra, as well as in West, Central and South Kalimantan. A few hotspots were also detected in Peninsular Malaysia and Java,” it added.
According to ASMC, air quality stations in areas affected by transboundary haze are also reporting moderate to unhealthy levels.
Meanwhile, data from Singapore’s National Environment Agency (NEA) showed that the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) in the central region had entered the unhealthy level at 102 as of 12pm.
Air quality elsewhere remained moderate, with the East and West recording a PSI of 91 each, followed by the North at 79 and the South at 82. — Bernama
fb1396e571801bac: KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Chong Motor Holdings Bhd has inked a three-year agreement with Perodua Sales Sdn Bhd to provide coating, painting and assembly line services for the national carmaker's battery electric vehicle (BEV) project in Serendah.

Its unit Tan Chong Motor Assemblies Sdn Bhd (TCMA) will provide electro-deposition (ED) coating and painting line services, as well as rental of a designated assembly line and related services for the project.
In return, Perodua Sales will pay TCMA service fees and rental charges.
The agreement, which commenced on June 1, has an initial tenure of three years, with Perodua Sales having the option to extend it for another two years.
The extension option must be exercised at least six months before the initial term expires.

Perodua Sales will be responsible for obtaining and maintaining the necessary approvals, permits and licences from the relevant authorities, as well as complying with applicable laws and regulatory requirements relating to BEV manufacturing.
It will also be responsible for maintaining and adequately insuring its equipment for the project.
Tan Chong said the project would have no effect on its issued share capital.
The project is expected to contribute to Tan Chong's revenue and earnings starting in the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026.
The agreement follows a letter of intent between TCMA and Perodua Sales announced on Nov 14 last year.
1d50df794cb59d37: JAKARTA: Indonesia is keeping 53 aircraft on standby to combat forest and land fires despite recording a significant decline in hotspots in Central and West Kalimantan, with nearly 600 hotspots still detected nationwide as fire risks persist.

Forestry Ministry Public Relations and Foreign Cooperation Bureau chief Dr Ristianto Pribadi said the decline in hotspots was a relatively positive development but cautioned that the fire threat remained.
"The decline in hotspots does not mean that all fires have been extinguished.
"The situation can change rapidly, especially when the weather is dry, winds are strong and combustible material remains on the surface," he said in the ministry's latest social media post on Monday.
According to the ministry's social media post, monitoring as of Sunday night detected 592 high-confidence hotspots nationwide, including 197 across the six priority provinces.
Central Kalimantan recorded 89 hotspots, followed by South Sumatra with 49, South Kalimantan 28, Jambi 17 and West Kalimantan 14, while none were detected in Riau.

On the ground and in the air, firefighting operations are continuing, with 53 aircraft on standby, including 34 for water bombing and 19 for aerial patrols and weather modification operations, Ristianto said.

The aerial response is also being reinforced by three CH-47 Chinook helicopters from Japan to support large-capacity water-bombing operations in areas requiring additional firefighting assistance, he said.

He said weather modification operations also continue in West and Central Kalimantan, contributing an estimated 87.9 million cubic metres of rainwater in West Kalimantan and 22.9 million cubic metres in Central Kalimantan as of Sept 11. — BERNAMA
4e341b916f6e3a5e: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The disclosure of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into the management and operations of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has triggered a series of investigations and legal proceedings, with a former minister becoming the latest person charged in court today.

Over the past several weeks, several individuals have been called in to give statements or detained to assist investigations, while five people have so far been charged at the Sessions Court here in connection with various cases.

In proceedings which began at 8.45am today, former Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here to three charges involving RM860,308,770.51 in TH funds.

Apart from Jamil Khir, those charged were former TH chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim, former THP Bina Sdn Bhd Security and Safety Manager Nasahruddin Ahmad, and former TH Properties Sdn Bhd deputy general manager Tengku Kamarolhisham Tengku Kamaruddin, who was also a former deputy general manager of THP Bina Sdn Bhd.
Also charged was Alam Maritim Resources Bhd group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Azmi Ahmad.
Here is the chronology of the RCI on TH:
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan says the proposal to make the final RCI report on TH public would be discussed at a Cabinet meeting.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim says the government was prepared to make the final RCI report on TH public in the near future to allow the public to know the findings of the investigation into allegations involving the sale of the agency’s strategic assets.
The Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) publishes the RCI report on the investigation into TH’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020.
The Prime Minister stresses that anyone found responsible for losses suffered by TH based on the RCI findings would be brought to justice.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) sets up a special team to review and scrutinise the RCI report on TH, which had been made public.
The Attorney General’s Chambers says it will immediately review the Commission’s findings.

b661bce98fa72684: PETALING JAYA: Seorang Ahli Parlimen Sabah menuntut Ketua Umno Sepang Noorazli Said memohon maaf kepada penganut Katolik susulan tindakannya membuat jenaka berunsur seksual membabitkan paderi serta rujukan yang tidak tepat mengenai Bible ketika Perhimpunan Agung Umno (PAU), baru-baru ini.
Dalam catatan di Facebook, Ahli Parlimen Tuaran merangkap Adun Tamparuli, Wilfred Madius Tangau, berkata jenaka itu 'amat tidak wajar dan menyinggung perasaan'.
"Kitab suci, paderi Katolik, dan biarawati tidak sepatutnya dijadikan bahan jenaka seksual atau dipersendakan dari pentas perhimpunan sebuah parti politik utama negara.

"Penceramah berkenaan sewajarnya mengakui kesilapan pertimbangannya, menarik balik rujukan palsu terhadap Mazmur 129, dan memohon maaf secara terbuka tanpa sebarang syarat kepada umat Katolik serta seluruh masyarakat Kristian," katanya.

Dalam ucapannya semasa membahaskan ucapan dasar presiden Umno pada Sabtu, Noorazli menceritakan jenaka mengenai seorang paderi yang memandu Proton Saga manual yang menawarkan tumpangan pulang kepada seorang biarawati, selepas melihatnya di di perhentian bas.

Setiap kali paderi itu menukar gear, tangannya tersentuh paha biarawati tersebut dan dibiarkan di situ, mendorong biarawati berkenaan mengingatkannya mengenai Mazmur ayat 129. Paderi itu kemudian menarik balik tangannya.
Setibanya di rumah, paderi itu menyemak Biblenya dan mendapati Mazmur 129 tidak mengandungi apa yang disangkakannya.

"Salah apa yang aku ingat ini...tuan-tuan nak tahu apa surah Mazmur ayat 129, dalam bahasa Inggerisnya dia cakap dengan izin - 'Go forth and seek further up and you will find glory'. Faham tak faham nie?
"Kalau tak faham saya terjemah dalam bahasa Melayu, jadi dia kata 'Teruskan usahamu kerana semakin ke atas semakin dekatlah kamu dengan kejayaan'," katanya.
Noorazli berkata, cerita itu adalah mengenai kepentingan untuk kekal fokus dan mengetahui apa yang ingin dicapai seseorang.
Beberapa pengguna Facebook di ruangan komen hantaran Tangau mendesak beliau untuk membuat laporan polis terhadap Noorazli, sambil menyatakan jenaka itu secara jelas menyentuh isu agama.
6adcf3889b0953eb: KUALA LUMPUR: Yes Group Management Bhd - a meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) specialist - has secured Bursa Malaysia's approval to list on the ACE Market.
The company, which traces its roots to 2008, started with corporate event planning before moving into domestic incentive travel in 2010 and overseas incentive travel in 2014.
It now provides customised incentive travel, event planning and management services to corporate clients.
The proposed initial public offering (IPO) comprises 91.87 million new shares and an offer for sale of 45.93 million existing shares, for a total offering of 137.80 million shares.
Of the new shares, 26.50 million will be offered to Malaysian public investors, 5.30 million allocated to eligible directors, employees and contributors under the Pink Form allocation.
A total of 60.07 million will be placed with Bumiputera investors approved by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry.
The offer for sale comprises 6.18 million shares for approved Bumiputera investors and 39.75 million shares for selected investors.
Post-listing, Yes Group's enlarged share capital will comprise 530 million shares.

According to its prospectus exposure, proceeds from the public issue will fund the expansion of ground transport services in Europe, the setting up of a UK regional office, establishment of Yes Academy, working capital and listing expenses.
The UK expansion is aimed at improving the group's control over pricing, costs and service delivery, while Yes Academy will focus on training tour leaders and managers.
Yes Group imanaging director Angela Mak Shau Kwan said over the years, it has grown from a travel and event solutions provider into a MICE specialist with strong execution capabilities.
236f34372b72d926: PUTRAJAYA: Jabatan Perkhidmatan Awam (JPA) sedang mengkaji inisiatif bagi menambah baik aspek pendapatan penjawat awam di negara ini, kata Ketua Pengarah Perkhidmatan Awam, Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz.
Beliau berkata gaji penjawat awam ketika ini tidak berada di bawah paras kemiskinan dan mereka dinasihatkan supaya bijak merancang perbelanjaan.
“Pada pandangan saya, penjawat awam dengan gaji yang ada sekarang ini tidak berada di bawah paras kemiskinan, cuma tinggal lagi bagaimana penjawat awam itu sendiri merancang perbelanjaan.

“Pada masa sama, kami juga sedang mengkaji perkara-perkara yang boleh memberikan ataupun menambah baik pendapatan penjawat awam,” katanya selepas merasmikan Persidangan Pengurusan Sumber Manusia Sektor Awam Tahun 2026.

Wan Dahlan berkata ketika ini, penyelarasan gaji penjawat awam telah dilaksanakan menerusi Sistem Saraan Perkhidmatan Awam (SSPA) dan segala inisiatif baharu tertakluk kepada kemampuan kewangan negara.
SSPA yang mula berkuat kuasa pada 1 Dis 2024 adalah inisiatif besar kerajaan bagi menggantikan Sistem Saraan Malaysia (SSM).
Ia diperkenalkan sebagai reformasi dalam perkhidmatan awam untuk meningkatkan motivasi kakitangan melalui struktur gaji yang lebih kompetitif serta penilaian prestasi yang lebih adil dan telus.

c5a423c52deb245e: DUBLIN: Ryanair Chief Executive Michael O'Leary on Thursday accused the head of Britain's air traffic control operator of lying about the cause of an outage that led to thousands of flight cancellations earlier this week.
O'Leary said Ryanair had been told by NATS Services Ltd that the outage was caused by a rogue flight plan, the same problem that caused a major disruption in 2023.
Speaking on BBC Radio on Wednesday, NATS CEO Martin Rolfe said he believed the latest outage had been caused by "something different" from previous incidents.
O'Leary, who has repeatedly called for Rolfe to resign, rejected that explanation.
"NATS have told us it was another rogue flight plan. Now Martin Rolfe is out denying it yesterday," O'Leary said. "I believe he's telling lies to save his own skin."

A NATS investigation into the 2023 outage found it was caused by a "one in 15 million" event in which a flight plan contained two identically named but separate waypoints, forcing both the system and its back-up into a "fail-safe" mode.

Responding to a similar statement from O'Leary on Wednesday, NATS said the latest outage had been caused by a different issue. It did not immediately respond to a request for comment on O'Leary's latest remarks.

Ryanair is suing NATS in London's High Court for more than £7 million (US$9.5 million) over the 2023 outage and has called on the operator to reinvest profits in performance improvements and staffing.
The government has given Rolfe a week to investigate the cause of the latest systems failure.

Transport minister Heidi Alexander, who summoned Rolfe for a meeting over the incident, said on Wednesday she believed the outage was avoidable and asked the Civil Aviation Authority to conduct an independent review.
3ac7d3c130bcdcf9: SHAH ALAM: A 15-year-old boy has been acquitted of murdering his 16-year-old schoolmate at a secondary school in Bandar Utama last year after the High Court today found him to have been of unsound mind during the incident.
Judge Adlin Abdul Majid ordered the boy to be detained and treated at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak at the pleasure of the Sultan of Selangor.

The boy's lawyer, Kitson Foong, who briefed reporters following the closed-door proceedings, said the court found that the requirements under Section 84 of the Penal Code, which provides for the defence of insanity, had been successfully established by the defence and that the prosecution had failed to rebut it.
13bfa9c526f1cbe6: BOGOTA: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella said Sunday he will challenge court orders blocking his hardline security policy.
De la Espriella has declared war on Colombia's myriad drug trafficking guerrilla groups, with his policy backed by US military support.
Since taking office last month, the right-wing leader has faced a string of legal setbacks.
A judge ordered De la Espriella's government to suspend bombings of guerrillas if intelligence indicated that minors were present.
An earlier court ruling halted the spraying of coca crops with a herbicide called glyphosate, which is linked to cancer in humans.
Another ruling ordered the president to hide graphic social media videos that appeared to show him walking among the bodies of alleged criminals.
"Judicial decisions are to be respected, and existing orders must be obeyed... but that does not mean giving up the right to challenge them," De la Espriella said in an address.
Colombia is the world's largest cocaine producer and is grappling with its worst violence in a decade.
The country has joined the Shield of the Americas, US President Donald Trump's anti-cartel alliance of Latin American countries, including Argentina, Ecuador and El Salvador.
4fbf5b1633a7081e: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Islamic Consumers Association (PPIM) and an activist have called for lawsuits to be filed against social media platforms for facilitating the online sale of drug-laced vapes to minors.

PPIM lead activist Nadzim Johan and social media influencer Ariz Ramli, known as Caprice, said such tech giants must be held accountable for the rampant sale of drug-laced vapes commonly known as "piu-piu".
They pointed to a suit filed by 29 American states against Meta over features on Facebook and Instagram that harmed children, which culminated in a historic US$18 billion settlement by the tech firm.
Nadzim and Ariz claimed that social media platforms had been "waiting for user complaints" over the sale of illicit vapes in the country instead of taking proactive measures.

They added that combating the drug trade requires a whole-of-society effort rather than relying solely on government agencies such as the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), health ministry or police.
They said the suits could be filed by members of the public, NGOs and even government agencies.
The activists demanded that social media platforms use their AI algorithms to detect and block illicit drug sales just as swiftly as they censored copyrighted material or sensitive speech.
The emergence of "piu-piu" has led to fresh calls for vapes to be banned in Malaysia.

In the first four months of 2026, police recorded 402 cases of drug-laced vapes, with synthetic drugs such as benzodiazepine, nimetazepam, MDMA, cannabinoids, tetrahydrocannabinol and methamphetamine detected.
533a27e0f3b1e4ab: SEREMBAN, Sept 14 — The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has declared that six individuals who signed a document dated September 5 seeking to depose the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan acted in a manner considered treasonous under adat and law.

The Dewan said four of the signatories did not hold the positions they claimed, had issued unlawful directives to government officers, and attempted to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir without the mandatory investigation required under the state constitution.

It ruled that no government officer should act on instructions based on the September 5 document, and directed the state administration to continue recognising Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar. The Dewan also instructed its secretary to lodge a police report against the six individuals, noting that four of them had signed the September 5, 2026 document without holding the offices they purported to represent.

The Dewan further expressed concern over a proposal to form a reconciliation committee under the state government, saying matters of adat fall solely under its jurisdiction as provided for in Article XVI of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution. It said it would seek clarification from the government on the committee’s terms of reference.

In its statement, the Dewan reaffirmed its July 31 decision that the proclamation dated April 19 was unconstitutional, as three of the four signatories were not recognised Undang at the time. It stressed that no investigation had ever been carried out, as required under Article X(1), and that Tuanku Muhriz had never been given notice or the opportunity to be heard.

The Dewan noted that the then menteri besar had refused to endorse the proclamation on April 20, rendering it void. It added that a subsequent attempt by a new menteri besar to sign the same proclamation did not revive it, as the function under Article X(2) had already been discharged.

It said announcements made on September 5 and September 8 had no effect, as they relied entirely on the flawed April 19 proclamation and a subsequent instrument dated August 3, which did not add legitimacy.

The Dewan emphasised that Tuanku Muhriz remains the lawful Yang di-Pertuan Besar and president of the Dewan, and that no vacancy exists. It also clarified the current holders of Undang positions: Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari (Sungei Ujong), Datuk Sedia Raja Haji Hassan Ab Hamid (Rembau), and Datuk Johan Pahlawan Lela Perkasa Setiawan Datuk Haji Muhammed Abdullah (Johol). The posts of Undang Luak Jelebu and Datuk Shahbandar Sungei Ujong remain vacant.

The Dewan concluded by urging all parties not to spread baseless claims about the institutions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar and the Undang, stressing that these adat institutions are a trust held for the people and heirs, not the property of any party or individual.
3b6f22a85e473956: PUTRAJAYA: The public services department is reviewing initiatives to improve the income of civil servants, director-general Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said today.
He said the current salaries of civil servants did not fall below the poverty line, and that they were advised to plan their spending wisely.
"In my view, civil servants earning their current salaries are not below the poverty line; it is simply a matter of how the civil servants themselves manage their expenses.

"At the same time, we are examining any measures that could provide for or further improve civil servants' income," he told reporters after officiating the Public Sector Human Resource Management Conference 2026 here.

Wan Ahmad Dahlan also said that salary adjustments for civil servants had already been implemented through the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), and any new initiatives would be subject to the country's financial capacity.
The SSPA, which came into effect on Dec 1, 2024, is a major government initiative that replaced the Malaysian Remuneration System.
It was introduced as a civil service reform to boost staff motivation through a more competitive salary structure and a fairer, more transparent performance assessment process.
4e7f2788168bee61: KUALA LUMPUR: Persatuan Pengguna Islam Malaysia (PPIM) dan seorang aktivis menggesa supaya saman difailkan terhadap platform media sosial kerana memudahkan penjualan vape yang dicampur dadah secara dalam talian kepada golongan bawah umur.

Aktivis PPIM Nadzim Johan dan pempengaruh media sosial Ariz Ramli, yang lebih dikenali sebagai Caprice, berkata gergasi teknologi ini mesti dipertanggungjawabkan atas penjualan berleluasa vape dadah, atau dikenali sebagai 'piu-piu'.

Mereka merujuk kepada saman yang difailkan oleh 29 negeri di Amerika Syarikat terhadap Meta berhubung ciri-ciri di Facebook dan Instagram yang memudaratkan kanak-kanak, yang akhirnya membawa kepada syarikat teknologi itu membuat penyelesaian bernilai USD18 bilion.
Nadzim dan Caprice mendakwa platform media sosial hanya 'menunggu aduan pengguna' berhubung penjualan vape tersebut di negara ini dan bukannya mengambil langkah proaktif.

Mereka menambah usaha membanteras perdagangan dadah memerlukan kerjasama seluruh masyarakat dan bukannya bergantung semata-mata kepada agensi kerajaan seperti Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM), Kementerian Kesihatan atau polis.
Sehubungan itu, mereka berkata saman boleh difailkan oleh orang awam, NGO dan juga agensi kerajaan.

Mereka turut menuntut platform media sosial menggunakan algoritma AI mereka yang canggih untuk mengesan dan menyekat penjualan dadah dengan pantas, sama seperti mereka menapis bahan hak cipta atau ucapan sensitif.
Kemunculan 'piu-piu' telah mendorong kepada gesaan baharu supaya peranti tersebut diharamkan di Malaysia.

Dalam tempoh empat bulan pertama 2026, polis merekodkan 402 kes vape dadah, dengan dadah sintetik seperti benzodiazepine, nimetazepam, MDMA, kanabinoid, tetrahydrocannabinol dan methamphetamine dikesan.
96cc973e88a674bb: BUTTERWORTH: A disabled man pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of sexually assaulting a 6-year-old girl inside a mosque.
Khairul Asyraf Hashim, 35, entered the plea after the charge was read to him before judge Rohaida Ishak.
He is accused of physically assaulting the child by touching her private parts for sexual purposes inside Masjid Jamek Haji Abdul Latiff in Permatang Pasir at 4pm on Sept 3.
The charge was framed under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Wan Amira Ruzaini Wan Abdul Razak did not offer bail due to the severity of the offence and the victim's young age.
"Although the accused is not related to the victim, he frequents the scene of the incident," she said.

In mitigation, National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Naqieya Zulkernain requested minimal bail, stating that the accused has a speech disability, is unemployed, and relies on his self-employed brother who has no fixed income.
"The flight risk is minimal as the accused attended court on his own and cooperated fully with the police," Naqieya said.
The court then ordered the accused to be sent to Hospital Bahagia in Tanjung Rambutan, Perak, for a mental health evaluation.
The court also fixed Oct 14 for mention.
It is understood that the victim was standing behind her father, who was performing prayers, when the incident occurred.
ae8bece6d8e5b215: PETALING JAYA: Lelaki orang kurang upaya (OKU) mengaku tidak bersalah di Mahkamah Sesyen Butterworth kerana melakukan serangan seksual fizikal terhadap seorang kanak-kanak perempuan enam tahun, di sebuah masjid, awal bulan ini.
Khairul Asyraf Hashim, 35, membuat pengakuan itu hadapan Hakim Rohaida Ishak.

Tertuduh didakwa melakukan serangan seksual secara fizikal terhadap mangsa dengan menyentuh bahagian sulit mangsa bagi tujuan seksual di dalam Masjid Jamek Haji Abdul Latiff di Permatang Pasir, dekat Butterworth, sekitar 4 petang, 3 Sept.
Justeru, Khairul dituduh di bawah Seksyen 14(a) Akta Kesalahan-kesalahan Seksual Terhadap Kanak-kanak 2017, memperuntukkan hukuman penjara maksimum 20 tahun dan sebatan jika sabit kesalahan.
Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Wan Amira Ruzaini Wan Abdul Razak tidak menawarkan jaminan atas alasan kesalahan tersebut serius serta mengambil kira mangsa yang masih kecil.
"Walaupun tertuduh tidak mempunyai hubungan kekeluargaan dengan mangsa, dia sering berada di lokasi kejadian," katanya menurut Berita Harian.
Peguam Yayasan Bantuan Guaman Kebangsaan (YBGK), Naqieya Zulkernain, mewakili tertuduh memohon jumlah jaminan minimum.
Beliau memberi alasan anak guamnya mempunyai masalah pertuturan, tidak bekerja, dan bergantung kepada abang yang bekerja sendiri serta tidak mempunyai pendapatan tetap.
"Risiko tertuduh melarikan diri adalah minimum kerana dia hadir ke mahkamah sendiri dan memberikan kerjasama sepenuhnya kepada polis."
Mahkamah kemudian memerintahkan Khairul dihantar ke Hospital Bahagia di Tanjung Rambutan, Perak untuk penilaian kesihatan mental, sebelum menetapkan 14 Okt ini bagi sebutan semula kes.
16ac776a898ec33a: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution today challenged his staff to design a kiosk operated by artificial intelligence (AI) that can translate any language and file a report with the Malaysian authorities in Bahasa Melayu.

The senator described the kiosk machine as a “dream” that he wants to see materialised by his ministry as the Anwar government pushes for broad artificial intelligence adoption in day-to-day operations.
“We must embrace AI and thank God we started this three years ago,” he said at the ministry’s monthly assembly here.

“Now we are in the phase of realising this adoption and if one of the dreams I have is when tourists come here, doesn’t matter if in KLIA, Bukit Bintang, and then disaster struck — their bags were snatched, or they lose their passports, or they are assaulted.

“They may be Japanese, Arabs. How do they lodge a report? My dream is there will be this kiosk machine. The tourists can speak in their own language and the AI machine will translate it, and write the report for them instantly in Bahasa Melayu,” the minister added.

Malaysia has been aggressively positioning itself as a regional AI hub, leveraging strategic infrastructure investments, tax incentives and public-private partnerships to attract multinational tech giants.

Major global players, including Microsoft, Google and Nvidia, have recently committed billions of dollars toward developing hyperscale data centres, cloud regions and advanced AI infrastructure across the country.
Johor and the Greater Kuala Lumpur region, in particular, have emerged as primary focal points for digital infrastructure expansion in South-east Asia.
Government leaders said the public-sector drive toward AI integration aligns with the administration’s broader National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2021-2025 and the Madani Economy framework.
Under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, the administration has urged civil servants to transition from conceptual AI strategies to practical, citizen-facing applications.
574a8712262fc6e6: SAN FRANCISCO: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on Sunday added his support to the idea of “pacing” AI development, so that cutting-edge models don’t outrun the ability of humans to maintain control.

Altman, echoing the language of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, said there’ll be a cost to this shift of focus to safety, but it’ll be worth it in order to maintain confidence that US companies are developing increasingly capable artificial intelligence responsibly.

“No amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring,” the OpenAI chief said in a post on X, emphasising also that the idea of ensuring safety doesn’t mean halting progress. “When we talk about ‘pacing’, we do not mean ‘stopping’.”

The comments come shortly after Amodei and SpaceXAI boss Elon Musk, in a rare moment of unity, called for tapping the breaks on AI development. Altman earlier this month told OpenAI staff that the startup is open to slowing advances in frontier technology to better understand the risks, and he has also confirmed that the company won’t go public in 2026 while prioritizing safety-related concerns.

AI-related stocks in Asia fell on Monday. Major OpenAI investor SoftBank Group Corp’s shares dropped 13% in Tokyo, while South Korea’s Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix both shed more than 4% in Seoul.

In his Sunday post on X, Altman reiterated OpenAI’s support for a federal AI framework, and said that AI firms need Washington’s help with international coordination, amid widespread concerns that even if US AI firms slow down their development, Chinese rivals will not do so.
978f80a3eec85b72: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia sedang mempertimbangkan tawaran Amerika Syarikat (AS) untuk menerima kapal kedua milik United States Coast Guard (USCG), kata Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

Bagaimanapun, beliau berkata keputusan hanya akan dibuat selepas Kementerian Dalam Negeri menerima laporan pemeriksaan bagi memastikan kapal berkenaan masih sesuai digunakan dan kos penyelenggaraannya munasabah.
Katanya, ketua setiausaha KDN akan mengetuai pemeriksaan bersama pakar Agensi Penguatkuasaan Maritim Malaysia (APMM), termasuk jurutera.
“Bila kita bawa balik (kapal yang pertama) tahun lepas...Dia kemudian menulis kepada saya untuk menawarkan kapal yang kedua.
“Jadi, pertama kita mesti buat pemeriksaan sendiri. Dia tawarkan satu bab. Kita sendiri kena puas hati,” katanya dalam sidang media selepas perhimpunan bulanan KDN.
Saifuddin berkata, tawaran kapal kedua itu dibuat selepas Malaysia menerima dan menggunakan kapal pertama.
Beliau berkata, kerjasama antarabangsa bukan sahaja membolehkan Malaysia memperoleh aset, malah merangkumi latihan, operasi bersama dan perkongsian risikan.
Katanya, penerimaan kapal pertama turut memerlukan kerja penambahbaikan, dengan sebahagian kos ditanggung AS.
“Jadi, kombinasi kos yang kita keluarkan dan yang dia bagi jumlahnya itu jauh lebih rendah berbanding pembelian satu aset baru. Jadi saya fikir itu kaedah yang munasabah,” katanya.
Bagaimanapun, Saifuddin menegaskan Malaysia tidak akan menerima tawaran itu jika pemeriksaan mendapati kapal berkenaan tidak lagi sesuai digunakan atau kos baik pulih terlalu tinggi.
Sementara itu, Saifuddin berkata Kementerian Kewangan secara prinsip bersetuju mempertimbangkan kenaikan elaun anggota Rela daripada kadar semasa RM8 sejam.
Katanya, lebih 35,000 anggota terbabit dalam tugasan termasuk mengawal kawasan larangan, membantu kawalan lalu lintas dan tugas keselamatan lain.
Beliau berkata, kadar baharu belum ditetapkan, namun perlu berada pada 'julat yang munasabah' mengambil kira kemampuan kewangan kerajaan.
Saifuddin berkata, kira-kira 1,300 anggota Briged Rela Siswa Siswi (Relasis) di universiti turut dicadang menerima elaun RM8 sejam bagi latihan mereka.
Katanya, mereka tidak menerima elaun sejak Relasis ditubuhkan pada 2017, dengan implikasi kewangan dianggarkan RM400,000 setahun.

Dalam perkembangan lain, Ketua Polis Negara, Mohd Khalid Ismail, berkata dakwaan Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan Ismail Lasim dipaksa menandatangani dokumen proklamasi bagi menurunkan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan masih dalam siasatan.
Katanya, kertas siasatan mengenai dakwaan itu sudah dibuka.
Saifuddin berkata, perkembangan lanjut akan dikongsi jika terdapat kemajuan dalam siasatan.
36057f5fed4d0422: KUALA LUMPUR: Harimau Malaya will face a familiar foe when they open their FIFA Asean Cup campaign against Bangladesh in Jakarta later this month, with former Sri Pahang coach Thomas Dooley plotting Malaysia's downfall.
The 65-year-old former United States captain, who coached Sri Pahang in the 2021 Super League, is leaving nothing to chance ahead of the Group A opener at the Gelora Bung Karno on Sept 25.

While Malaysia's centralised training camp under interim coach Tan Cheng Hoe begins on Sept 21, before the team flies to Jakarta the following day, Bangladesh have already been put through an intensive residential camp at the Kings Arena in Dhaka.
Dooley has also trimmed his preliminary 28-man squad to a travelling party, giving them more time to prepare tactically.
"We have only two more weeks. You cannot focus on the final 23 if you have 30-plus players in camp," Dooley said.
"Those travelling to Indonesia need the workload and tactical attention."
Bangladesh are scheduled to arrive in Jakarta on Sept 19, almost a week before the match, giving them time to acclimatise to the conditions at Senayan.
Sanctioned by FIFA and held during the men's International Match Calendar window, the 14-nation tournament features Southeast Asian sides and invited teams.
The format leaves little room for error, with only the group winners advancing directly to the Oct 5 final while the runners-up contest the third-place playoff.
After Bangladesh, Malaysia face hosts and arch-rivals Indonesia at Senayan on Sept 28 before travelling to the Si Jalak Harupat Stadium in Bandung to meet Singapore on Oct 1.
With no semi-final safety net, a slip-up against Bangladesh could severely damage Malaysia's hopes of topping Group A.

Harimau Malaya may be the higher-ranked side on paper at 136th compared to Bangladesh's 181st, but Dooley's early preparations and knowledge of Malaysian football ensure their opening test in Jakarta will be anything but straightforward.
Sept 25: Bangladesh v Malaysia, Gelora Bung Karno Stadium, Jakarta
Sept 28: Malaysia v Indonesia, Gelora Bung Karno Stadium, Jakarta
Oct 1: Malaysia v Singapore, Si Jalak Harupat Stadium, Bandung
9829b8904c4898c8: PETALING JAYA: A Sabah MP has called on Sepang Umno chief Noorazli Said to apologise to the Catholic community for making a sexual joke about the clergy as well as a false reference to the Bible at the recent Umno general assembly.
In a Facebook post, Tuaran MP and Tamparuli assemblyman Wilfred Madius Tangau said the joke was "grossly inappropriate and offensive".
"Sacred Scripture, Catholic priests and religious sisters should not be sexualised or ridiculed from the stage of a major national political party.
"The speaker should acknowledge his poor judgment, withdraw the false reference to Psalm 129 and offer an unqualified public apology to the Catholic and wider Christian community," he said.
Several Facebook users in the comments section of Tangau’s post urged him to lodge a police report against Noorazli, saying the joke clearly touched on matters of religion.
"Religion is not a joke. How would it be if others joked about his religion? This is a 3R (race, religion and royalty) offence. Lodge a police report," said user Ricardo Rozales.
4255617f698da339: DUBAI: The number of international tourists visiting Dubai dropped by 44% year-on-year in the first eight months of 2026 amid escalating tensions in the Middle East, according to data from Dubai’s economy and tourism department, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.

Ahead of the annual Arabian Travel Market exhibition in Dubai, officials released data on tourist numbers for the first time since February. Previously, such figures had been published on a monthly basis.
In the first eight months of 2026, the city welcomed 6.97 million international tourists, including 869,000 in August, the highest monthly figure since February, the Dubai Media Office said.
Monthly performance reports for Dubai’s tourism sector, available on the department’s website, show that 12.54 million tourists visited the city between January and August 2025.
Consequently, tourist arrivals fell by more than 44%, representing a drop of nearly 5.6 million people in absolute terms.
In 2025, Dubai welcomed a record 19.6 million international tourists.
Dubai authorities aimed to transform the emirate into a year-round tourist destination and one of the world’s top three tourism hubs.
Amid regional tensions and flight cancellations after the escalation in February, many hotels in Dubai closed for renovations.
280032280652fc98: TOKYO, Sept 14 — A candidate backed by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s ruling party won a gubernatorial election in Okinawa, bringing to power a leader who approves of a contentious US military base relocation plan for the first time in 12 years.

In a landslide victory following yesterday’s vote, Genta Koja beat incumbent Denny Tamaki, who has long pushed for a major US military base to be moved out of Okinawa, Japan’s southernmost prefecture.
Koja, 42, accepts a central government plan to keep the US Marine Corps’ Futenma air base on Okinawa’s main island, but move it to a less populated location.

His campaign focused on economic messages, pledging to double Okinawa’s average income, the local government budget for childcare, and spending by tourists on the island, which has long been less prosperous than the rest of the country.
Denny Tamaki (2nd L) speaks to media after reports projected his defeat in the Okinawa gubernatorial election, in Naha, Okinawa prefecture on September 13, 2026. — AFP pic
He pledged today to “make progress on livelihood issues, the economy and childcare assistance” by listening to views of all Okinawan residents.
Takaichi told reporters in Tokyo that she would “do my utmost to coordinate efforts with the new governor to strengthen the Okinawan economy”.
“As for other subjects, I will address those after hearing from the new governor,” she said.
The US military presence will remain a major issue for Koja, a former civil servant who was also a deputy mayor of Naha, the region’s capital city.
The US has around 54,000 military personnel stationed in Japan, mostly on Okinawa, but a string of incidents over the years, including sexual assault cases, have angered residents.
Other base-related woes, from pollution to noise and helicopter crashes, have led to further complaints.

Japan and the US agreed to move the base from the town of Ginowan to another location within Okinawa in 1996 after a rape of a 12-year-old schoolgirl by US military servicemen that triggered strong anti-US military protests across the prefecture.
The relocation plan was approved in 2013 by Okinawa’s then governor Hirokazu Nakaima, but the next year he lost to an opponent who opposed the move.
Tamaki, 66, was seeking his third term yesterday.
Koja won 423,124 votes, while Tamaki received 276,060, according to the prefectural government. — AFP
d4e2a9bd8ffcd659: NEW DELHI: India's interior minister has vowed to further implement a contentious common civil code for states governed by the ruling Hindu nationalist party, a move expected to stoke concern among minority Muslims.

India's 1.4 billion people are subject to a common criminal law, but rules on personal matters such as marriage, divorce and inheritance vary based on the customary traditions of different communities and faiths.
The introduction of a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) to replace those diverse rules has been a long-standing goal of prime minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
At least four states have implemented the UCC so far.

"We have introduced the UCC in several states... I am confident that we will implement (it) in all 21 states governed by the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance by 2029," Home Minister Amit Shah said on Sunday.
The campaign for a standardised civil code has raised concerns, especially among Muslim citizens, who say such a move would infringe on their religious freedoms.

Supporters say the UCC gives Muslim women the same rights as others by ending polygamy, setting equal property inheritance rights for sons and daughters, and requiring divorce processes to take place before a civil court.
India, the world's most populous country, is majority Hindu. It is also home to an estimated 220 million Muslims, giving it the world's third-largest Muslim population.
India's next national elections are due in 2029, after Modi won a third successive term in 2024, when he was forced into a coalition government.
5a94b9fd435bab02: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia will receive the second of two Multi-Purpose Mission Ships being built in Turkey for the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) by the end of next year, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
The timeline marks an acceleration from Saifuddin's earlier statements, which had indicated the vessels were expected to arrive by early 2028.
Saifuddin said he will travel to Istanbul at the end of this month to personally access the progress of both vessels.
"The first vessel will arrive in March next year — one month before Lima (Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition). The second vessel will be by the end of next year.
"And that will be a source of pride for MMEA. New assets will boost the morale of the fleet. That is important," he told a press conference after the ministry's monthly assembly here today.
332e4254cbe0e40f: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA) is calling for 2027 Budget to tackle what it sees as an uneven playing field between local retailers and foreign e-commerce platforms, while easing rising operating costs.

Ahead of the budget's tabling by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 9, MRCA called for stricter enforcement of the sales tax on low-value goods and equal treatment of cross-border online sellers.
It said foreign platforms offering ultra-low-priced goods were putting pressure on local retailers, while differences in tax and compliance obligations could erode Malaysia's tax base.
MRCA also urged stronger action against counterfeit and substandard goods sold online, citing concerns over consumer safety, product quality and intellectual property protection.
On business costs, the association sought an exemption from the six per cent service tax on utility supplies paid by commercial tenants through mall management.
It said taxing utility payments that are merely passed through to tenants created an additional cost burden.

MRCA also proposed tax rebates or double deductions for retailers and commercial property operators investing in environmental, social and governance upgrades, particularly fire safety and infrastructure.
It wants the service tax on construction and renovation services cut to three per cent, arguing that construction materials are already taxed.
MRCA also renewed its call for the gradual reintroduction of the Goods and Services Tax, using a phased approach over five-year intervals to give businesses and consumers time to adjust.

To support domestic demand, MRCA called for sales taxes on locally manufactured goods removed and the RM1,000 domestic tourism tax relief extended through 2027 to cover hotel stays and selected retail spending.
MRCA said a more predictable policy and tax environment would reduce compliance costs, support investment and strengthen the competitiveness of Malaysian retailers.
4a76e4c1a27550bc: QUITO, Sept 14 — Argentine manager Marcelo Gallardo has been appointed as the new head coach of Ecuador for the 2030 World Cup qualifying campaign, the nation’s football federation announced yesterday.
The 50-year-old won multiple trophies as manager of Argentine club side River Plate, but has not previously managed an international side.
He replaces his compatriot Sebastian Beccacece, who stepped down after Ecuador’s disappointing loss to co-hosts Mexico in the first knockout round of this year’s World Cup.

“We sought out Marcello Gallardo for what he has won, but above all for what he represents. Welcome to Ecuador, Marcelo,” said Francisco Egas, president of the Ecuador Football Federation (FEF), in a video posted on social media.
Known for his attacking style, Gallardo is the most successful coach in the history of River Plate with 14 trophies in his first stint, including two Copa Libertadores wins.
But his recent, second spell at River Plate was a disappointment. He stepped down following a poor run of form in February after failing to win any further trophies.
Ecuador have become a major force in South American football in recent years, finishing second in qualifying for the 2026 World Cup, after Argentina.
They boast international stars including Arsenal’s Piero Hincapie and Paris Saint-Germain’s Willian Pacho. — AFP
ceb43bd12bf08464: KOTA KINABALU: Croatian climber Mauro Persic has expressed deep remorse over the risks he took after spending eight days alone and injured on Mount Kinabalu, while saying the ordeal renewed his faith in humanity.
The 46-year-old said the rescue had humbled him, particularly after rescuers and porters had to carry him down the mountain when he became too weak and injured to continue on his own.
Among those who left the deepest impression was a porter whom Persic estimated to be only 15 years old.
As the teenager carried him downhill, Persic said he could feel every impact through the young porter's legs and knees.
"It broke my heart. Was it all worth it? I don't know. Probably not. Broken body. 40 people risking their lives to save one," he wrote in a Facebook post.
Persic said the people who came to his aid, many of whom were strangers, treated him with extraordinary kindness throughout the ordeal.
Instead of leaving him bitter, however, the experience strengthened his belief in human compassion.
He said the rescuers and locals brought him food, chocolate and snacks, gathered around a campfire, shared jokes and kept him company while the rescue operation was underway.
"I've seen the very best of humanity showing up these days; generosity, kindness and care," he said.
He also expressed gratitude to the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department, saying: "Last gratitude from my heart to Bombas who I owe my life. You are all my brothers from another mothers."
Persic, who was rescued by a multi-agency team last week, sustained injuries to his right leg and ribs, as well as minor cuts to his hands, in the incident.

The climber, who took part in an extreme adventure race in the Tambatuan area of Kota Belud less than a fortnight ago, had ascended Mount Kinabalu via an eastern route, a trail linking villages that depend on spring water sources in the Kundasang area.

Despite the hospitality shown by locals, Sabah Deputy State Secretary Datuk Jamili Nais said those who violated Mount Kinabalu's regulations should face jail time as a deterrent against others entering the sacred mountain illegally.
Jamili, who previously served as Sabah Parks director and was responsible for the management of the mountain, said stern action was needed to deter similar violations.
As of press time, Persic remained under police detention while receiving treatment at a private hospital here.
Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Arifin said investigations were still ongoing.
